title_en: Fragments from the Book against Diodore of Tarsus
author: Cyril of Alexandria
occasion: The surviving fragments come from Cyril's work against Diodore of Tarsus. They preserve a passage from a homily by Cyril on Matthew 24:29-36, in which he explains the saying that no one knows the day or hour, not even the Son.
argument: Cyril argues that when Christ says no one knows the day or hour, not even the Son, he does not precisely mean the divine Son of God. The disciples were overreaching in trying to learn the depths of the Lord, so Christ speaks in a veiled way. The saying means that even a human being called to adoption as a son, a renewed human being, should not seek what is beyond nature. Since the Father has not revealed it even to angels, no human being will know it, even if called to adoption.

outline.move: Cyril introduces the homily on Matthew 24:29-36 and argues that 'not even the son' does not precisely mean the Son of God, because the disciples were overreaching in trying to learn the depths of the Lord.

Cyril explains that Christ spoke in a veiled way so that by not refusing the explanation they wanted to learn, he would not seem to grieve those showing themselves genuine, saying no one knows, not even the angels, not even the son, except the Father.
Cyril interprets the saying to mean that even a human being called to adoption and shown to be a new son should not seek what is beyond nature or expect to learn what the Father has not revealed.
Cyril concludes that if an angel does not know, no human being will know, even if called to adoption.

The addressee is not stated in the surviving fragments.
The full structure and scope of the original treatise cannot be reconstructed from these fragments.
Diodore's specific views are not stated in the surviving Greek fragments; he is named only in the Latin title.

_unresolved_facts.claim: They preserve a passage from a homily by Cyril on Matthew 24:29-36
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Κυρίλλου ἐν ὁμιλίᾳ ἐπιγεγραμμένῃ εἰς τὸ Εὐθέως δὲ μετὰ τὴν θλίψιν τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐκείνων
_unresolved_facts.fix: The fragments preserve a passage from a homily by Cyril on Matthew 24:29 (specifically beginning with the lemma 'Εὐθέως δὲ μετὰ τὴν θλίψιν τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐκείνων'), not the full range Matthew 24:29-36. The citation covers only the saying about the sun being darkened and the unknown day/hour (Matt 24:29, 36), not verses 30-35.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Cyril argues that when Christ says no one knows the day or hour, not even the Son, he does not precisely mean the divine Son of God.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οὔτε γὰρ προσέθηκεν ἀκριβῶς Οὐδὲ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἀλλ' ἀπολελυμένως Οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός φησιν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Cyril argues that Christ did not add precisely 'not even the Son of God' but spoke in an absolute/unqualified way 'not even the son' (without the article or 'of God'). The point is about the precise wording Christ used, not about whether Christ 'meant' the divine Son. Cyril's argument is grammatical/philological: the lack of precision in the wording allows for a different interpretation.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The saying means that even a human being called to adoption as a son, a renewed human being, should not seek what is beyond nature.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: εἰ καὶ κέκληται πρὸς υἱοθεσίαν ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ υἱὸς ἀνεδείχθη νέος
_unresolved_facts.fix: Cyril interprets 'son' (υἱός) as referring to a human being who has been called to adoption and shown to be a 'new son' (υἱὸς νέος), not 'a renewed human being.' The emphasis is on the newness of sonship through adoption, not on renewal of the human being. The adopted human is called 'son' in a new sense, parallel to but distinct from the divine Son.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Cyril introduces the homily on Matthew 24:29-36
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Κυρίλλου ἐν ὁμιλίᾳ ἐπιγεγραμμένῃ εἰς τὸ Εὐθέως δὲ μετὰ τὴν θλίψιν τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐκείνων
_unresolved_facts.fix: Cyril introduces the homily on Matthew 24:29 specifically (the lemma 'Εὐθέως δὲ μετὰ τὴν θλίψιν τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐκείνων'), not the range 24:29-36.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Cyril explains that Christ spoke in a veiled way so that by not refusing the explanation they wanted to learn, he would not seem to grieve those showing themselves genuine, saying no one knows, not even the angels, not even the son, except the Father.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἵνα τοίνυν μὴ ἀπαγορεύσας τὴν ἐξήγησιν ὡς ἠβούλοντο μαθεῖν, δόξῃ πως λυπεῖν τοὺς γνησιεύοντας, ἐπεσκιασμένως φησί
_unresolved_facts.fix: Cyril explains that Christ spoke in a veiled way (ἐπεσκιασμένως) so that by NOT refusing the explanation as they wished to learn it, he would not seem to grieve those showing themselves genuine. The brief inverts the logic: Christ veils his speech precisely to avoid the appearance of refusal, not as a refusal itself. The 'not' (μὴ) governs ἀπαγορεύσας, making this a negative purpose clause—'so that by not refusing...'

_unresolved_facts.claim: Cyril interprets the saying to mean that even a human being called to adoption and shown to be a new son should not seek what is beyond nature or expect to learn what the Father has not revealed.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἀλλὰ μὴ ζητείτω τὰ ὑπὲρ φύσιν, μηδὲ ἀξιούτω μαθεῖν ἅπερ μηδὲ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Cyril interprets the saying to mean that a human being called to adoption and shown to be a new son should not seek what is beyond nature, nor should he consider himself worthy (ἀξιούτω) to learn what [the Father has not revealed even to angels]. The brief's 'expect to learn' misses the sense of ἀξιούτω ('deem worthy'/'claim entitlement to'), which carries a stronger tone of presumption or claiming a right to knowledge.

_unresolved_facts.claim: In frag-rem-early, φησί introduces Cyril's interpretive expansion of Christ's veiled manner of speaking, not a direct quotation of Matthew.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἐπεσκιασμένως φησί "Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ἢ τῆς ὥρας, οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ "οἱ ἄγγελοι, οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός, εἰ μὴ ὁ
_unresolved_facts.fix: In frag-rem-early, φησί introduces a direct quotation of Christ's words (with Cyril's interpretive expansion): 'About that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels, not even the son, except the...' The quotation marks in the source indicate direct speech, and the content matches Matthew 24:36 with Cyril's expanded elements. It is not merely 'interpretive expansion' but a presented quotation of what Christ said (with the variant reading).

_unresolved_facts.claim: The opponent named only in the Latin title of the work, not in the surviving Greek fragments.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Fragmenta ex libro contra Diodorum Tarsensem
_unresolved_facts.fix: The opponent is named in the Greek title/heading as well: 'Fragmenta ex libro contra Diodorum Tarsensem' is the Latin/Greek title given at the head of the fragment. The title is in Latin, but it is part of the transmitted source text, not a separate Latin tradition. The claim that Diodore is 'named only in the Latin title' misleadingly suggests a distinction between Latin and Greek transmission that is not relevant here—the title is the title of the fragment collection as transmitted.
